description: Establishment of the National Regulatory Reform Council to strengthen Regulatory Governance for Small and Medium Enterprises
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-18 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - Sri Lanka’s regulatory environment plays a pivotal role in shaping growth of private sector, influencing investment decisions and enhancing overall business competitiveness. Although the country’s economic fundamentals are strong, it has been observed that the existing regulatory constraints disproportionately affect Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and have also had adverse effects on Sri Lanka’s attractiveness as an investment destination. Taking into account these matters, the Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, in collaboration with the Asian Development Bank, has conducted a comprehensive assessment of Sri Lanka’s regulatory framework and, following extensive consultations with relevant stakeholders, has developed the National Regulatory Reform Action Plan and its implementation mechanism. The said Action Plan has put forward a set of practical and actionable recommendations, which have been prioritized and sequenced across short-term, medium-term and long- term horizons. Further, it has also been proposed to establish a National Regulatory Reform Council as the central institutional mechanism for guiding and overseeing the implementation of the said Action Plan. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development to establish the said Council under the Chairmanship of the Hon. President and to designate Ministry of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development as its Secretariat, was approved by the Cabinet.
